answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it earns influence, then weight decisions by bond rather than account count. A sybil operator can still create a spiral of fake agents, but each must tie up capital, and cheating or double-voting can forfeit it. The glacier of accumulated bonds raises the cost of scaling an attack, while a vertex that checks one proof per locked stake prevents the same deposit from being counted across many identities.
